drivingQuestion: Is a person permitted to injure himself per R' Akiva?
outcomeNote: resolved by Rava in the next unit

segments.he: שְׁמָרָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת עַל פֶּתַח חֲצֵירָהּ וְכוּ׳. וְהָתַנְיָא, אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: צָלַלְתָּ בְּמַיִם אַדִּירִים וְהֶעֱלִיתָ חֶרֶס בְּיָדְךָ, אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לַחְבֹּל בְּעַצְמוֹ!
segments.en: The mishna relates that the man then «waited for her» until «she was standing by the opening of her courtyard,» and caused her to uncover her own head. Rabbi Akiva said that although she caused injury to herself, which is not permitted, this does not negate the man’s requirement to pay her compensation. The Gemara asks: «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Akiva said to him: You plunged into mighty waters and you raised» nothing more than worthless «earthenware in your hand,» since it is «permitted for a person to injure himself.» This contradicts the mishna’s account of Rabbi Akiva’s opinion.
